text: thats why we diversify
I've paired schd with schg and schy. It seems to work well. I'm a beginner and it has taught me a few things
I like SCHD alot but it really needed to be paired with a growth focused ETF.
The downside is real. SCHD caps your upside. You're giving up growth for income. In a raging bull market you'll watch growth funds leave you behind.
I have held SCHD for years and the underperformance during growth rallies stings. Hard to stay patient when everyone else seems to be getting richer faster.
The part people miss is that SCHD's yield isn't guaranteed. Companies can cut dividends. If you're relying on that income you're exposed to risks nobody mentions. Small miscalculations compound.
Schd & Spym is a great combination. 8% overlap & a very low expense ratio of 0.08%

I have 800+ shares within my ROTH IRA, plan to buy more shares with my ROTH, DCA over the next 12 months, with DRIP set from 10/2027  to 10/2032. My focus is to keep up with inflation, invest in dividend paying ETF/stocks and capital preservation. Any other suggestions?
